blocks.text: Bulbus cordis is located at the cranial end of the developing heart tube, not the caudal end.

The endothelial heart tube is derived from the splanchnopleuric mesoderm, located near the pericardial cavity. (Option A) Initially, the heart appears as right and left endothelial heart tubes. These tubes fuse to form a single heart tube.
The heart tube has 5 dilatations, which are:
**Sinus venosus** is located at the caudal (venous) end of the primitive heart tube. It consists of a body with two prolongations known as the right and left horns.

items.text: **Right horn:** Forms smooth part of the right atrium (sinus venarum).

blocks.text: Each horn receives blood from three veins:
Bulbus cordis is the cranial most part of the developing heart tube. (Option C) Forms outflow (smooth) parts of the right ventricle (conus arteriosus) and left ventricle (aortic vestibule).
**Primitive ventricle:** Forms inflow (rough) parts of both ventricles.
**Primitive atrium:** Forms trabeculated part of the right and left atrium.
**Truncus arteriosus:** Forms ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk. (Option B)

items.text: **Heart Tube Folding:** Brings the arterial and venous ends closer together.
Disappearance of the dorsal mesocardium creates the transverse sinus of the pericardium. (Option D)
Parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium become continuous at the arterial and venous ends of the heart.
One enclosing the aorta and pulmonary trunk.
Other enclosing the SVC, IVC, and four pulmonary veins.

blocks.text: Two tubes are separated by the transverse sinus of the pericardium.
